q: My cat is a real hunter; she _______ anything that moves.
We _______ the next ECL four weeks from today.
My aunt _______ in the Egyptian Navy for six years.
My teacher _______ to the graduation ceremony tomorrow.
Both of us _______ a ghost last night on the back stairway of the hotel.
My grandkids _______ the Internet right now, so you can’t use the phone line.
Craig and his family _______ in Buenos Aires last year.
Your mother _______ from Valencia airport two hours ago.
According to the drill instructor, the trainees _______ the barracks.
Yesterday, I _______ to the movies.
By this time next year, I _______ all my exams.
While I was driving to work this morning, I _______ about my briefing.
Before the firemen could extinguish the flames, the house _______ already burnt down.
First, I went to the movie, then I _______ some pizza.
When I was a child, I always _______ my homework.
Before I went to bed last night, I _______ my teeth.
Because it was raining, we _______ the picnic.

We _______ already.
I _______ your ideas, and I regret to say I cannot accept them.
They _______ there since December.
We _______ since three o’clock.
I _______ to him, but he _______ yet.

q: It _______ three months, and I _______ my glasses yet.
Mrs. Pemberton _______ that her chauffeur prefers rock music.
The next-door neighbor’s dog _______ me.
You _______ too late, Doctor. The poor girl _______.
She _______ travelling by bus, and he _______ travelling by car either.
o: has always detested, has never liked
is always detesting, is never liking
will always detest, will never like

q: Fiona _______ the Loch Ness Monster five times.
A bee _______ me!
The workers _______ building that factory.
I’m going to leave in half an hour. I _______ all of my work before I _______.
I’m going to eat lunch at 12:30. After I _______ lunch, I _______ a nap.
I’m going to watch a TV programme at nine. Before I _______ that programme, I _______ a letter to my parents.
I _______ here until he _______.
As soon as the rain _______, I _______ to the shop.
Bridget and Ross got married on June 1st. Today is June 14th. They _______ married for two weeks.
This traffic is terrible. We _______ to the airport late.
You look really great! _______ at the fitness center?
If I _______ the change light, I would have stopped.
This weekend, we _______ near Lake Placid.
You _______ that shirt for tonight’s party.
Mum _______ the food for the party.
We _______ you again next week.
They _______ preparations by the time the guests arrived.
The delegation _______ the visitors at the airport tomorrow.
We _______ skis here since 1964.
Nobody _______ Tiger Woods at golf yet.
They _______ German at EU meetings.
The Chinese _______ acupuncture thousands of years ago.
_______ he _______ you back the book yet?
The boy _______ the cake right now.
Dad _______ me a box of chocolates.
The spider _______ her yesterday.
The guide _______ us the Natural History Museum this afternoon.
The government _______ that petrol prices will rise tomorrow.
A burglar _______ into our house last week.
The fruit-pickers _______ the apples early in the morning.
It’s time the authorities _______ something about this problem.
Lots of people _______ their cars on the pavement yesterday.
The government _______ with the report and _______ the law.
Hardly had the alarm sounded ______ the crew reached their stations.
e: Hardly ... when.

q: No sooner had he arrived ______ the briefing began.
e: No sooner ... than.

q: It was not until 1998 ______ the treaty was ratified.
e: It was not until ... that (emphatic structure).

q: Only after the inquiry ______ the truth.
e: Inversion after Only after.

q: Little ______ that the mission would change everything.
e: Inversion after Little.

q: The officer, ______ report we read, has been promoted.
e: Possession -> whose.

q: I'd rather you ______ the classified file open.
e: would rather + subject + past simple.

q: He objected to ______ without notice.
e: object to + V-ing (passive).

q: They made him ______ the report again.
e: make + *sfv*.

q: The document needs ______ before Friday.
e: need + V-ing carries a passive meaning.

q: Were I in command, I ______ the order.
e: Inversion = if I were.

q: Had we known earlier, we ______ differently.
e: Third conditional with inversion.

q: Not only did he refuse, ______ he also resigned.
e: Not only ... but also.

q: We had the radio ______ yesterday.
e: have something done.

q: Provided that he ______ on time, we will proceed.
e: Provided that + present.

q: He is the only officer ______ speaks fluent Arabic.
e: Human subject, so who.

q: Despite ______ exhausted, he completed the patrol.
e: Despite + a noun or an -ing form (despite being exhausted).

q: Under no circumstances ______ the perimeter.
e: Inversion after Under no circumstances.

q: The briefing lasted ______ longer than expected.
e: much + comparative.

q: He accused the petty officer ______ negligence.
e: accuse sb of.

q: Scarcely ______ the port when the storm broke.
e: Inversion after Scarcely.

q: A device for circulating air to cool a room is _____.
e: A fan has blades that rotate and circulate air, cooling the air of the room.

q: An octopus is so-named because it has eight _____.
e: The eight "arms" of the octopus are called *tentacles*.

q: When you finally get back home, please _____ me a postcard.
e: *Imperative*. A request. "You" is omitted from the main clause.

q: Because of the rain, the Base Commander _____ the parade.
e: *Future*. He hasn't done it yet. *He will do* it.

q: If I _____ you, I would study more.
e: "Would study" means this structure is the *present unreal* among the "*If*" clauses.

q: My brother, but not his sons, _____ coming to visit me next week.
e: *Brother is*

q: Because he was driving while intoxicated, Craig _____.
e: clause should be simple past. *He got* (passive) *he got arrested*. *He got promoted*. *He got robbed*.

q: If you had been here yesterday, you _____ my wife.
e: "*If*" clause. *Past unreal* because of "yesterday."

q: The man _____ by the door is my uncle.
e: This is a reduced clause. The man (who is) sitting by the door

q: There _____ a bad series of accidents near Highway 64 and Loop 275 yesterday afternoon.
e: subject is "*A series*." *A series was*

q: If you don't get a high score on the next ECL, you _____ in trouble.
e: *Future* "*If*" *Clause*. The word "next" indicates this.

q: It is mandatory that Capt. Barrow _____ in Maj. Whitfield's office at 0730.
He enjoyed _____ soccer.
e: The verb "*Enjoy*" requires gerund ( "-ing" form after it.

q: He didn't actually hit me, but he _____ at me twice with a baseball bat.
e: irregular verb *swing swung*

q: I am scheduled for another ECL next week, _____?
e: I am, aren't I? This is a strange structure, but that's the way it is.

q: Someone might have to stay in the office until 1800 if _____.
e: This is a fixed structure. If need be. *If* the *need* should *be* for something, and we reduce it to *if need be*.

q: She likes fish, doesn't she? Yes, but she dislikes beef, _____?
e: tag has to be negative.

q: Kudos _____ to anyone who can answer all of these questions correctly.
e: be "praise."

q: All of the furniture _____ by the floodwaters.
e: "Furniture" is a mass noun. Mass nouns take singular verbs.

q: _____the barking dogs, we would not have been alerted about the fire in our house.
o: If it would not be for
e: A reduced "*If*" clause. If it had not been for the barking dogs, We drop the "If" and reverse the subject and first auxiliary verb.

q: A species of rare fish _____ on display at the Larkspur Museum.
e: species is

q: I finally got the dog _____.
e: You *get* somebody *to do* something. (infinitive)

q: It is my understanding that the subject the students in IDS enjoy the most _____ preposition usage.
e: "The subject" is the simple subject of this sentence.

q: We were putting up our tents when it _____.
e: gerund. *It began to snow* or *it began snowing*.

q: When I was a child, I used to _____ cats.
e: Here "used to" is followed by simple form.

q: _____, I would not have gone to that disco last night.
e: Reduced "if" clause. If I had been you Had I been you

q: The President can, it is widely believed, in no way, resolve this crisis soon,_____?
e: The phrase "in no way" makes the main clause negative, so the tag must be affirmative.

q: If I had not eaten so much pizza last night, I _____ so sick right now.
e: This is a mixed structure "*If*" clause. The time words "last night" and "right now" something *had not happened* last night.

q: At least one species of fish _____ extinct every week.
e: *One species* = singular subject We need a singular verb. One species becomes extinct.

q: Craig will have been working for this company for 25 years by the time he _____.
e: time she finally moves to a bigger house, she will have been living in this one for 40 years.

q: Class starts _____ 0730.
e: When you have an exact time for something, you use "At." The movie ended at :45.

q: My uncle lives _____ a farm.
e: *On* a farm. On base. On a reservation.

q: We will have another ECL _____ Tuesday.
e: A day by itself gets *on*.

q: We will leave _____ noon.
e: Specific exact time. At noon. At 12:00.

q: I am not talking _____ you! I'm talking _____ Capt. Barrow.
e: You talk *to* a person.

q: I went _____ Jordan for a two-week vacation.
e: You go *to* a place.

q: Class will start _____ 0730.
e: specific time

q: He will graduate _____ July 23.
e: When you have a specific day indicated by *number*, you use *on*.

q: I didn't understand what he said _____ me.
e: We say something *to* a person.

q: The test will start _____ 0745.
e: Exact times take *at*.

q: He is staying _____ the Hilton Hotel.
e: You stay *at* a place.

q: Capt. Larsen comes _____ a small country called Lentavia.
e: You *come from* a certain place.

q: I will meet you in Lab 4 _____ exactly 0736.
e: Exact times need *at*

q: They honeymooned _____ Brussels.
e: Cities take *in*. So do countries, counties, towns

q: His party will be _____ Sunday.
e: Day of the week by itself

q: The teachers always gives too much homework _____ us.
e: You *give* something *to* somebody.

q: The President lives _____ 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue.
e: The number is given along with the street name. Use *at*.

q: He told some jokes _____ me.
e: You *tell* something *to* someone.

q: We will have another test _____ Friday.
e: day of the week by itself

q: She was born _____ Estonia.
e: We use "*In*" for countries. I was once stationed *in* Jordan.

q: I like my coffee _____ milk and sugar.
e: One thing combined *with* another thing or *with* other things.

q: I always take my big vacation _____ the summer.
e: *In* a season of the year

q: My car is parked _____ the red Toyota and the white Cadillac.
e: We use "between" when we are taking about *two* specific things.

q: Don't laugh _____ other people's mistakes.
e: We laugh *at* things and people.

q: I am tired _____ studying prepositions.
e: We say we are *tired of* something.

q: Please don't talk _____ someone else's speech.
e: We *talk during* an event.

q: Is your ID card _____ your wallet?
e: It would be *in* or *inside* a wallet. In a drawer. In a closet. In a box.

q: There were five passengers _____ the car when it got hit by the train.
e: We are *in* a car.

q: Please listen carefully _____ the instructions.
e: We *listen to* something.

q: I have not heard _____ family lately.
e: You hear *from* people when you get any kind of letter, phone call, e-mail

q: All of the passengers are _____ board the plane now.
e: *On board* is a phrase meaning inside a larger vehicle like a plane, train, bus, ship.

q: Hurry up! We will wait _____ you here.
e: You *wait for* someone or something.

q: A submarine is designed to function _____ the water for long periods of time.
e: "Sub" is a prefix meaning "under," so it follows that a submarine can function *under* the surface of the water.

q: I went _____ high school in Ponce.
e: You *go to* school. *Go to work go to* just about any place.

q: We will talk to you _____ the supervisor's office.
e: When you talk about a specific room, you use *in*.

q: Last night, I slept _____ 9 hours.
e: total amount of time

q: I think he has a knife _____ his pocket.
e: *In* a pocket *in* a purse *in* a drawer

q: May I borrow $300 _____ you?
e: You *borrow from* someone. You can *loan to*. You can *lend* to.

q: I ordered chicken _____ rice.
e: Two things linked together coffee *with* cream salad *with* dressing ice cream *with* chocolate sauce

q: She is the supervisor _____ Unit 6.
e: noun *of* noun structure or association Queen *of* England chief *of* trainees leader *of* Delta Company

q: I always brush my teeth _____ going to bed.
e: time element *before* or *after* doing something

q: Their new business will be located _____ Fulton Street.
e: Name of the street by itself. No address number given.

q: He stabbed me _____ a dirty kitchen knife.
e: *With* indicates the weapon used. Cut the bread *with* that clean knife, not *with* that dirty one.

q: The policeman showed his badge _____ me.
e: You show something *to* someone.

q: There was nothing _____ the envelope when I opened it.
e: *In* or *inside* certain objects like envelopes, pockets, purses, wallets, drawers, boxes

q: May I ride _____ the airport with you?
e: You *go to* a place, so you can *ride to* a place.

q: I want another glass _____ milk.
e: Something and the item of measurement used for it.

q: I lived in Oregon _____ 13 months.
e: Total amount of time is given.

q: I will not vote _____ him.
e: You *vote for* or you *vote against* something or somebody.

q: I want to ask you some questions _____ your family.
e: You can *ask about* a subject.

q: That shelf is too high. You need to stand _____ a chair to reach it.
e: You stand *on* something for added height.

q: Take these pills _____ a glass of warm milk.
e: Two items together.

q: I want to talk to you _____ a few minutes.
e: amount of time is given Use *for*

q: You can't go swimming in the river _____ the winter.
e: *In* one of the four seasons

q: What is the job _____ a drill instructor?
e: association noun *of* noun The role *of* a leader

q: He hit me _____ his dictionary, and it was the first time he had ever used it for anything.
e: The tool or weapon is given. He shot me *with* a rifle.

q: Who do you think you are The Queen _____ England?
e: noun *of* noun structure the King *of* Fools the Governor of Nevada

q: I can't eat anything fried _____ butter.
e: You can cook things *in* or *with* butter, oil, margarine

q: My unit will not be _____ the parade tomorrow.
e: You are *in* a parade.

q: Divide these cookies _____ all twelve students in this class.
e: *Among* for more than two

q: Why is he under investigation _____ the FBI?
e: agent under suspicion *by* the police under surveillance *by* the cops

q: She gave a party _____ her class, all of whom enjoyed themselves.
e: You can give an activity *for* someone give a party *for* me give a baby shower *for* my sister

q: The teacher divided the candy _____ all the students of the class.
e: Remember: *between* is for *two* things. *Among* is for more than *two*.

q: The river runs _____ the old bridge.
e: The water will pass *under* the bridge under normal conditions.

q: The dog jumped _____ the bed with his muddy paws.
e: You can *jump on* a higher surface.

q: That window is so dirty that I can't see _____ it.
e: From one side to the other involves *through*. *See through* the fog. *See through* the dirty windshield.

q: He was shot twice in the back _____ a Colt.45.
e: We use *with* to indicate what method, tool, or instrument was used.

q: He got _____ an argument with his neighbor.
e: You can *get into* certain things: into trouble into an argument get into debt

q: This umbrella will not protect you _____ heavy rain.
e: We *protect from*

q: Some of the best stores in Boston are located _____ Newbury Street.
e: *Trick question*? The name of the street is Newbury Street. The actual number of located *at* 645 Newbury Street. The stores are on Newbury Street.

q: I live _____ the third floor of the dorm, the smoking floor.
e: Something is *on* a certain floor of a building.

q: We have to photocopy this contract, so write your name _____ black ink, not blue.
The cat is hiding _____ the bed.
e: The only one that conveys the idea of *hiding* is *under*.

q: What is the reason _____ his failure?
e: We would have a *reason for* something.

q: He is currently enrolled _____ a two-year college.
e: You enroll *in* a school.

q: You must stay today _____ 3:30.
e: *Stay until* a certain time is reached.

q: Scissors are used _____ cutting paper.
e: for -ing Something is used to cut Used (in order) to do something

q: The robber snuck up _____ me and held a gun to my back.
e: If he sneaks up and touches your back, he has to be *behind* you.

q: The train travels _____ the tunnel at 90 miles per hour.
e: A tunnel is like a long tube, so something travels *through* it.

q: The children are playing _____ the backyard.
e: It's a place with a perimeter or border.

q: When will Capt. Barrow be able to retire _____ the Army?
e: You *retire from* a job.

q: We will participate _____ the parade next week.
e: You participate *in* an activity.

q: My mother is the lady seated _____ the blue sofa in the corner.
e: *In* a chair (with arms) *on* a chair (without arms) *on* a sofa (because it's wide and you might not be touching the arms of it).

q: It is difficult _____ me to speak in front of the class.
e: Something is *difficult* or *easy for* you.

q: He is an outspoken critic _____ his country's economic policies.
e: noun *of* noun structure a champion *of* human rights a defender *of* freedom a critic *of* reforms

q: The contractors are going to tear _____ the old abandoned house.
e: The building is standing *up*, so you have to tear it *down*.

q: Capt. Barrow got a 98 _____ his last test.
e: You achieve a score or get a grade *on* a test.

q: What should I do _____ a sore throat?
e: treatment You do something *for* a headache. Or *about* a *cold*.

q: It was _____ a cool evening in late June that I first met him.
Do you live _____ base in the dorms?
e: We say *on base* versus *off base*. Another example would be *on* a reservation versus *off* a reservation.

q: Please write the rough draft of your essay _____ pencil.
e: in ink in pencil If you want to use "with," you have to say "with A pencil.

q: This cake is made _____ eggs, butter, milk, chocolate and nuts.
e: made of made from made with made out of If you want to use "made by," it's passive: made by a person made by using ingredients or utensils.

q: This sketch of my mother was made completely _____ memory.
e: *From* memory also - *by memory*

q: The paratroopers jumped out of the plane _____ hesitation.
e: We do things either with or without hesitation.

q: I was a little late for my appointment, but I still got there _____ time for the doctor to see me.
He blamed the accident _____ me.
e: You *blame* something *on* someone.

q: He blamed me _____ the accident.
e: You *blame* someone *for* doing something wrong.

q: We will provide him _____ a new dictionary if he has lost his old one.
e: You *provoide* someone *with* something.

q: The troops have been standing _____ parade rest for 20 minutes.
e: Drill positions: stand at ease, at attention, at parade rest.

q: I did it _____ accident.
e: You do something *by* accident.

q: What I am asking _____ you is that you be quiet during other people's speeches.
e: You *ask* something *of* someone. What I'm asking *of* you is that you do your homework.

q: Did you have the right to ask that question _____ him?
e: You ask something *of* someone. I need to ask a favor *of* you.

q: His broken nose should not have a negative influence _____ his ability to swim in the final race.
e: One thing can have an influence *on* another thing.

q: He comes to school every day _____ an old motorcycle.
e: He is sitting *on* top of it.

q: He comes to school every day _____ motorcycle.
e: method of transportation *by bike by horse* but -- *on* a bike on a horse (Look for the article "A" or "*An*.")

q: I found a great 3-bedroom apartment, so I'm going to move_____ base.
e: You either live *on* base or *off* base. So you would move *off* base.

q: She wore a veil _____ her face.
e: "Over" can mean to *cover* something. He held his hand *over* his mouth.

If you _____ to DLI to study English, what language would you have liked to have studied?
One would think that if Aristotle _____ your father, you would have been happy.
Should you ever be taken as a POW, _____ only your name, rank, and serial number.
If he _____ speaking English, it's news to me. I thought he was speaking Icelandic.
e: *Past real*. He really *was* speaking English.

q: I asked Craig again if the accident _____ his fault.
e: *Past real* The accident *was* Craig's fault. He just keeps denying it.

q: If there _____ a point to his speech, I missed it entirely.
e: *Past real* The speaker claims there *was* a point to his speech. I just didn't understand it.

q: The student next to me tried to copy from my paper. He was trying to_____.
e: To copy someone else's answer is *cheating*.

q: He stabbed his victim with a _____.
e: You would *stab* with a knife, not with the other 3 objects.

q: The train will arrive _____ 0955.
e: specific exact time

q: A dog usually likes to chase cats, and a cat usually likes to chase_____.
e: Cats would chase mice, not the other 3 objects.

q: He had to go to the hospital because he had an _____.
e: Only "accident" makes sense here.

q: The Empire State Building is located _____ New York City.
e: Something is *in* a city *in* a country *in* a town

q: My father died _____ April 17, 1989.
e: specific date Use *on*.

q: If the water is frozen, it is _____.
e: Water freezes and becomes *ice*. (Steam and boiling are associated with *hot* liquids.)

q: I have been at DLI _____ 6 months.
He is such _____ honest person.
e: The "h" of "honest" is silent, so it sounds like "*Onest*," a vowel sound. He is *an honest* person. She is *an honorable* person.

q: Did you _____ a big breakfast this morning?
e: Anytime you use the *do*" auxiliary, put simple form of the verb. *Do* you *go* to the gym every day? *Did* he *see* that movie?

q: Most officers who live at DLI cook _____ own food in microwave ovens.
e: *Possessive* adjective form. It is *their* food. (The subject --officers -- is plural.)

q: He wants to know whose book this is. I tried to tell him that it's_____.
e: possessive pronoun. Whose hat is that? It is *mine*. It is *my* hat.

q: _____ knows Ellen's brother.
e: The verb "knows" needs a third person singular form.

q: That television show was _____.
e: The show was *boring*. I was *bored* when I watched it.

q: Today's class was _____ than yesterday's.
e: comparison more fun than

q: The police _____ coming to investigate the robbery in just a few minutes.
e: *Police* = plural The police are.

q: No matter where you live, you need _____ access to a hospital.
e: "Access" is a noun. Modify it with an adjective. What kind of access? *Quick* access.

q: I need to go to the bank because _____.
o: I want to cash a check.
e: Bank should involve *money*. *Cash* a *check* for the *money*.

q: I want _____ to a movie tonight.
e: "want" is followed by an infinitive. The student *wants to look at* page 4-19 versus verbs followed by gerunds.

q: Whose book is that?
e: possessive adjectives. It's my book. Or It's mine. (possessive pronoun)

q: Why is the baby crying? Because _____.
e: Of these four answers, the only thing to explain a baby's crying would be the *hunger*.

q: Capt. Barrow _____ 8 more weeks before he graduates.
e: *Still* is not a verb. It an adverb. Capt. Barrow *has* 8 more weeks. He *still has* 8 more weeks.

q: He offered _____ me move my heavy furniture upstairs.
e: "Offer" is followed by an infinitive. See Book 34 p-4-19 for a big list of verbs followed by infinitives versus gerunds.

q: The cheetah ran _____ that the photographers couldn't take pictures.
_____ you are rich, you can pay for everyone's lunch.
That's the man _____ shot the bank guard.
e: subject form of the relative pronoun. I saw the man. *He* shot the guard. I saw the man *who* shot the guard.

q: Of my four brothers, Danny is _____.
e: four people? Use the superlative. He is *the tallest* one of the four.

q: I don't have _____ money to go to the movie tonight.
e: mass noun The main clause is negative, so "I don't have *enough* of something to do it." I don't have enough time to iron my shirt.

q: During the flight from Orlando, I felt very _____.
e: adjective form I was *nervous*. I felt *nervous*.

q: I didn't have _____ money to pay for my movie ticket.
I hate spinach, and _____.
e: abridged agreement I hate something and so does my brother. I hate something and my brother does too.

q: He went down the hall _____.
e: We need an *adverb* ( -ly form) because it tells us *how* he went down the hall. Adverb of manner.

q: That shirt, _____ is light blue, costs less than $15.
e: "Which" is used for things. A shirt is a thing. "Who" and "whom" are only used for people.

q: Before _____ your test paper, verify that you have answered all the questions.
e: hand in" is *handing in*. Before *leaving* your room, I make sure the door is locked.

q: She's the _____ student in our class.
e: *Superlative form* good better best. It takes "the." This is *the hardest* test I have ever seen.

q: I hope I can go up ten points _____ the next ECL.
e: You get a score *on* a test.

q: You need _____ experience if you want a job in this company.
e: Here, "experience" is a mass noun. You need some of it.

q: Last night, I _____ too much Pepsi.
e: irregular verb *drink drank drunk*

q: I am _____ tired to go to the movie with you tonight.
I need _____ a car for the weekend.
e: The verb "need" requires the infinitive form in this structure.

q: The reason for his many absences _____ difficult to understand.
e: The reason is the subject and it is singular

q: That was the _____ movie I have ever seen.
e: superlative form of the adjective "good." *Good better best*

q: He keeps _____ my comb!
e: After the main verb "keep," you need to put the "-ing" form of a word. *Keep studying* and you will do fine.

q: She is very _____.
e: You need an adjective here. "Studious" is the adjective form of "study.

q: If you leave ice cream out in the sun, it will _____.
e: When frozen stuff starts to warm up, it *melts* (*thaws*).

q: Craig bought a new car in Cleveland. He paid cash for *it*. The word *it* refers to_____.
e: pronoun reference He bought a car. He paid for *it*. *It* refers to the car.

q: The wind is _____ very hard.
e: The wind *blows*.

q: Dikes, dams, and levees are all intended to control _____.
e: If you check your dictionary, you'll find that these are all engineering structures constructed to hold back large amounts of water.

q: The guerrillas caused problems _____ the government.
e: You *cause problems for* someone.

q: I didn't eat _____ yesterday.
e: double negatives! You must not say "I didn't eat nothing."

q: I am not _____ for writing the scores in the records.
I had the secretary _____ the letter five times.
e: You have somebody *do* something (simple form). I had the barber *cut* my hair *cancel* my credit card.

q: Would you mind _____ the door for me? My hands are full.
e: "mind" takes gerund (-ing) form after it.

q: We will try to play the soccer game _____ the rain.
e: You can use either *despite* or *in spite of*. There is no such phrase as *despite of* or *in spite*.

q: I made _____ mistakes on this test than I did on the one last week.
e: fewer mistakes *mistakes* is a count noun. This is a comparative structure. I have *fewer* problems now than I did when I was a teenager.

q: If you want to mail that letter, you will have to use three _____.
e: When you turn a number into part of a hyphenated adjective, you drop the plural of the *mile* run

q: He promised me that he _____ repair my car tomorrow.
e: past of *will* is *would*.

q: Of my two sons, Danny is _____.
e: You are comparing *two* things (people). *Old* is just one-syllable. Put -*er* after the Danny is *the older* of the two sons.

q: He studied English at Harvard _____ two years.
e: He did something *for* a measurable amount of time. Lincoln was President *for* five years.

q: While _____ the street, be very careful to look in both directions.
e: This is a reduced structure: *while you are crossing the street* reduce it to *while crossing the street*.

q: Mrs. Barrow is a great painter, and _____.
e: The main clause contains the "*Be*" verb, so the second abridged clause must also

q: We will start the test _____ Cpl. Whitfield gets here.
e: "As soon as" has the meaning of "when" in this sentence.

q: They took his car to the shop _____ it.
e: They did it *in order to fix* it. We can reduce it: *they did it* (in order) *to fix* it.

q: When I was a child, I used to _____ candy all day long.
I want to tell you about some interesting _____ places you should visit when you come to my country.
e: A place for tourists to visit is a tourist place. Don't use the word "touristic.

q: I think these questions are the _____ of all the questions I have tried.
e: *Superlative* : The adjective is 3 syllables long, so you must use "*Most*" to express car I have ever seen. She is *the most intelligent* person I have ever met.

q: _____ continuously, the dog nearly drove me crazy.
e: This is a reduced structure. It started out as the clause "Because it was barking continuously," and we can reduce it to "Barking continuously.

q: There _____ a lot of hard questions in this particular exercise.
e: The verb must agree with "hard question." A lot of hard questions *are* in this exercise.

q: He has _____ accent.
e: "you-neek." He has *a unique* accent.

q: Florida used to be a major _____ outpost.
e: The adjective form of "Spain" is "Spanish."

q: The witness avoided _____ the truth about his involvement in the robbery.
e: Put the " - ing" form after "avoid." He avoided *falling* because he grabbed a hold of the railing.

q: I don't recall _____ you before.
e: Put "ing" form after "recall.

q: Neither the animals nor their keeper _____ killed in the fire.
The cause of all the recent accidents at several major airports_____ not been determined yet.
e: *Cause* is the simple subject. The verb must agree with *cause*. The *cause has* not been determined.

q: Neither the captains nor the Commander _____ going to be at ECO today.
e: *For* structure where one element is singular and the other is plural, make the verb agree with the element closer to it. Neither the father nor his sons *are* here right now.

q: I anticipate _____ back home.
e: Put a gerund ( -ing form) after *anticipate* or *look forward to*.

q: The money _____ from the bank has not been recovered yet.
e: This is a reduced clause structure. The money *which was stolen from the bank* can be reduced down to *the money stolen from the bank*.

q: _____ the test, he stood up and left the room.
e: This started out as the clause *after he had finished the test* We can reduced it to the phrase *having finished*

q: _____ you're up, would you get me the bag of potato chips?
e: *As long as* introduces a condition. It means provided that, or since.

q: The thunderstorm knocked out the electricity, thereby _____ impossible for us to watch TV.
e: *Angering* all the students.

q: _____ a foreign language is difficult.
e: An infinitive can be the subject of a sentence. So can a gerund. *To run* is good exercise. *Running* is good exercise.

q: _____, the student left the testing room.
e: Reduced clause. "After he had finished" can be reduced to the phrase "Having finished.

q: The drill instructor is very angry. He is _____.
e: angry = upset = mad = furious = very unhappy

q: You *have to* increase your ECL score by at least 6 points or else!
e: modals *have to* = *must* requirement mandatory

q: We really *ought to* go home now.
e: modals ought to = should (advice, recommendation)

q: Why is Craig *lame*? He _____.
e: *Lame* means walking with difficulty because of problems with a leg, a foot, an ankle, the toes.

q: He *drowned*. He _____
e: *Drown* = to die by suffocation in liquid

q: If you *double the radius* of a circle, you get the _____.
e: *Radius* = half of the diameter

q: If I have no friends, I am probably _____ at times.
e: Lonely = alone = not with other people

q: He is *elderly*. His age is around _____.
e: elderly = old = aged

q: Is the material *flammable*? _____ No, it is _____.
e: flammable = it *will* burn *no*Nflammable = it will *not* burn Do not be flames. *Flammable* and *inflammable* mean the *same thing*!

q: I ate a _____ for dessert.
e: *Pear* = a fruit, similar to an apple (usually sweet and yellow)

q: His family is not rich. In fact, they are very _____.
e: not rich = poor = not wealthy = not much money

q: Don't *gripe* so much.
e: *Gripe* = complain = say negative things = kvetch

q: Video cameras are used in many stores to _____ shoplifting.
e: *Deter* = to try to prevent something from happening

q: Soldiers are always *griping*.
e: gripe = complain = make negative comments

q: I can't take a shower because the _____ is broken.
e: nozzle = the end of a pipe or a hose that allows you to control the flow of water.

q: You pay the rent to the _____.
e: *Landlord* or *landlady* = the person who owns property and charges people rent.

q: I have _____ about question #2.
e: *A doubt* = an uncertainty = not knowing something

q: He drew a quick _____ of the crime suspect.
e: *Sketch* = a quick drawing = a picture that one draws quickly

q: I fell down because someone _____ me from behind.
e: *Shove* = push

q: A hatchet is _____.
e: hatchet = a small ax used for chopping

q: Hot and cold air is conveyed through a _____.
e: *Duct* = a tube, channel, or pipe for the passage of liquids or air. What did the ancient Romans use an *aqueduct* for?

q: His jeans are *faded*. They _____.
e: *Fade* = losing the color, colors are not bright like they used to be

q: He is a *tightwad*. He is _____.
e: *Tightwad* = stingy, miserly, doesn't want to spend his money. (Wants to keep all of his paper money rolled in a tight wad, without ever having to spend any of it.)

q: That painting is counterfeit! It's an obvious _____!
e: *Counterfeit* = fake = not genuine = bogus = phony = not real

q: When you go outside, you have to _____ your hat.
e: *Put on* clothing = to wear clothing = to don an item of clothing

q: I was looking for my car keys when I _____ my father's antique hunting knife.
e: *Run across* = to find something unexpectedly, especially when looking for something else.

q: What is your opinion of this book? What do you _____?
e: *To think of something* = to have an opinion. You just saw that new movie, didn't you? What did you think of it?

q: I have to give a speech tomorrow. I _____ give a speech.
e: "*Have to*" = "*Must*." Modals

q: The Titanic is lying two-and-a-half miles _____ the surface of the water.
e: *Beneath* = *under* = *below* = *underneath*

q: We have a certain lack _____ discipline in this unit.
e: noun *of* noun structure *excess* of *students* opposite *lack* of *students*

q: The paramedics arrived at the crash site _____ time to save dozens of victims.
e: *In* time, not *on* time. *On* time suggests there was an appointment. In time means they were not too late to do something.

q: My brother is _____ debt. He owes thousands of dollars to some loan sharks.
e: *In* debt opposite *out of* debt

q: There are only 9 people _____ the bus right now.
e: *Aboard* means to be on a large vehicle like a plane, bus, train, ship, space shuttle

q: He comes to class every morning _____ foot.
e: means of transportation *on* foot *but by car by bicycle*

q: I like to sit _____ all the flowers.
e: *Amidst* = among (old-fashioned poetic)

q: We have to take another test on Friday. We _____ take another test.
e: modals *have to* = *must*

q: You *ought to* see the movie Saving Private Ryan as soon as possible. You _____ see that movie.
e: modals ought to = should (recommendation/ advice)

q: The last test was not easy. In fact, it was extremely _____.
e: not easy = difficult = hard

q: That bird looks very *unusual*. Yes, it looks _____.
e: unusual = strange = not ordinary = not common

q: We're going to be late for the ECL. We *have to* hurry.
e: modals *have to* = *must*

q: There was a chemical spill in the *tail* of the jet. The spill was in the_____.
e: tail = rear = aft = back part = (ship) stern

q: Is this CD player very expensive? _____ No, it is _____.
e: Opposite of expensive = cheap costly = expensive

q: The boss is very *angry*. She is _____.
e: *Angry* = upset, not happy, not pleased

q: The weatherman says it *may* rain tomorrow.
e: modals *may* = *might* (possibility)

q: Mrs. Goodteacher has _____ students at DLI in her Advanced Class.
e: good = better = best Something is *the best*.

q: Don't give the new students too _____ things to do their first week in class.
e: count noun = things *too many things* versus *too much work* (mass noun)

q: Do you think he *is able to* get the job done by himself?
e: modals *can* = to be able

q: The price of that sofa is very low. The sofa is _____.
e: low price = cheap = doesn't cost much

q: Our ECL scores are low. We *must* study.
e: modals *must* = have to = mandatory = requirement

q: The graduating class _____ a party next week.
e: *Next week* = future The class *will* do something *next week*.

q: What is the *subject* of her speech?
e: subject = topic = what you are talking about

q: Curtis is deaf. He _____.
o: has no hair on his head
e: *Deaf* = cannot hear

q: She gave the police a good _____ of the robber.
e: noun form = a description

q: Capt. Arroyo's date of _____ is April 23.
e: noun form = departure = the act of departing or leaving

q: I thought the movie was terribly good. I _____.
e: terribly = awfully = *very* = extremely terribly good = very good terribly bad = very bad

q: Craig had _____ trouble when he tried to take a bus downtown.
e: *Trouble* = a mass noun *much* trouble *lots* of trouble *a lot of* trouble *too much* trouble

q: The traffic was extremely heavy. There were _____ cars on the road.
e: *Cars* = count noun Heavy traffic means *too many cars*.

q: Craig looks very ill. He _____ go to the doctor right now!
e: modals Should = advice If he's sick, he should go to the doctor.

q: How did she hurt herself? She _____ down when the bus made an abrupt stop.
e: *Fall fell fallen* (simple past = *fall*)

q: When snow starts cascading down the side of a mountain, we call it_____.
e: avalanche = snow falling rapidly down the side of a mountain

q: The cake is *tasty*. It is _____.
e: tasty = tastes good = delicious

q: If the water is vaporized, we can call it _____.
e: vapor = steam Choices A, B, and D all involve *cold*. Only C involves *heat*.

q: It is raining; _____, I want to play soccer outside.
e: *Still* = but, yet, however *still* can be used for *contrast* structures

q: I became sick; _____ I didn't want to take the test.
e: thus = therefore = hence A formal word used with a semicolon.

q: If he is lame, he probably has trouble _____.
e: lame = something wrong with the leg or foot

q: We cannot wade across the river because it is _____.
e: wade = to walk, usually with the water not higher than your knees.

q: He looked at me _____ he didn't understand a word I was saying.
e: as if = in such a manner like

q: I am scheduled to take one more OPI, _____?
e: exception I AM, *aren't I*? More formal = I AM< *AM I not*?

q: The ambassador's wife wants to eat in _____ restaurant.
e: The movie was 4 hours long. = It was a four-hour movie. The book is 300 pages long. = It is a 300-page book.

q: When will you retire _____ the military?
e: We retire *from* a job.

q: He is not old _____ to join the military yet.
e: She is smart enough to join *mensa*.

q: You can count on Capt. Arroyo because he is such a _____ person.
e: count on = depend on = rely on The adjective forms would be *dependable* and *reliable*.

q: He considers himself better than other people. He _____ them.
e: *Look down on* = to think one is better than other people, to treat other people as inferiors, to think one is *higher* in standing than other people

q: My glass is empty. Please _____ again. I'm thirsty.
e: *Fill* up = replenish = put something in an empty space

q: He was *raised* by his grandparents after his parents' death.
e: *Bring up* = raise = help something to grow (This one is in the passive voice.)

q: Why do you always keep your coat _____?
e: two-word verb *keep* (clothing) *on* opposite: *take* (clothing) *off*

q: You can always rely _____ Capt. Barrow to help you.
e: two-word verb *rely on* = *depend on*

q: I want you to accompany us. Come _____ with us.
e: phrasal verb come along with

q: I fell down when I was trying to run away _____ the pit bull.
e: phrasal verb to *run away from* something

q: He was a bad father, so the social services agency took _____ his children.
e: two-word verb *take away* = remove

q: Last night, we dined _____ lobster and shrimp.
e: dine on = to eat formal

q: Can we go _____ you to the movies?
e: go along with = phrasal verb meaning to accompany

q: We could hear the *faint* sound of a child's voice calling for help.
e: (adjective) faint = very soft (verb) faint = pass out = black out = lose consciousness

q: He was just so old and tired that his poor little heart _____.
e: *Give out* = to stop working, to cease functioning The engine finally gave out after about 120,000 miles.

q: The two ministers don't see eye to eye on defense spending. They:
e: See eye to eye = agree. Negative form = disagree.

q: Don't jump _____ conclusions.
e: You jump *to* conclusions. (It's a set phrase.)
